q-41549.name: Question 1
q-41549.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $16$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot 2,$ and the $20(y-3)$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 5\cdot (y-3).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{16}{20(y-3)}=\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot 2}{2\cdot 2\cdot 5\cdot (y-3)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there are two pairs of $2$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot 2}{2\cdot 2\cdot 5\cdot (y-3)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot \cancel{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2}{\cancel{2}\cdot \cancel{2}\cdot 5\cdot (y-3)} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2}{5\cdot (y-3)} & = \\ \frac{4}{5(y-3)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{4}{5(y-3)}.$

q-75370.name: Question 2
q-75370.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $18a$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 3\cdot 3\cdot a,$ and the $9(a+2)$ in the denominator becomes $3\cdot 3\cdot (a+2).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18a}{9(a+2)}=\frac{2\cdot 3\cdot 3\cdot a}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a+2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there are two pairs of $3$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 3\cdot 3\cdot a}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a+2)} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot a}{\cancel{3}\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot (a+2)} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot a}{a+2} & = \\ \frac{2a}{a+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{2a}{a+2}.$

q-155.name: Question 3
q-155.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $2(x-1)$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot (x-1),$ and the $2(x+1)$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot (x+1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x-1)}{2(x+1)}=\frac{2\cdot (x-1)}{2\cdot (x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is only one pair of $2$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot (x-1)}{2\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot (x-1)}{\cancel{2}\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{(x-1)}{(x+1)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{x-1}{x+1}.$

q-155.html:
Question 3
?

2(x−1)2(x+1)=

a
x+1
b
1
c
2(x−1)(x+1)
d
x−1x+1
e
2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The 2(x−1) in the numerator becomes 2⋅(x−1), and the 2(x+1) in the denominator becomes 2⋅(x+1).

2(x−1)2(x+1)=2⋅(x−1)2⋅(x+1)

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is only one pair of 2's.

2⋅(x−1)2⋅(x+1)=2⋅(x−1)2⋅(x+1)=(x−1)(x+1)

Thus, the expression simplifies to x−1x+1.

q-75369.name: Question 4
q-75369.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $12(x-1)$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1),$ and the $15x$ in the denominator becomes $3\cdot 5\cdot x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12(x-1)}{15x}=\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1)}{3\cdot 5\cdot x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $3$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1)}{3\cdot 5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot (x-1)}{\cancel{3}\cdot 5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2\cdot (x-1)}{5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{4(x-1)}{5x}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{4(x-1)}{5x}.$

Question 4
?

12(x−1)15x=

a
2(x−1)5x
b
4(x−1)5x
c
5(x−1)4x
d
x−1x
e
2(x−1)3x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The 12(x−1) in the numerator becomes 2⋅2⋅3⋅(x−1), and the 15x in the denominator becomes 3⋅5⋅x.

12(x−1)15x=2⋅2⋅3⋅(x−1)3⋅5⋅x

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of 3's.

2⋅2⋅3⋅(x−1)3⋅5⋅x=2⋅2⋅3⋅(x−1)3⋅5⋅x=2⋅2⋅(x−1)5⋅x=4(x−1)5x

Thus, the expression simplifies to 4(x−1)5x.

q-57766.name: Question 5
q-57766.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $10x$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 5\cdot x,$ and the $12(x+1)$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10x}{12(x+1)}=\frac{2\cdot 5\cdot x}{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $2$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 5\cdot x}{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 5\cdot x}{\cancel{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{5\cdot x}{2\cdot 3\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{5x}{6(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{5x}{6(x+1)}.$

q-57766.html:
Question 5
?

10x12(x+1)=

a
5x6(x+1)
b
3x4(x+1)
c
xx+1
d
56
e
4(x+1)3x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The 10x in the numerator becomes 2⋅5⋅x, and the 12(x+1) in the denominator becomes 2⋅2⋅3⋅(x+1).

10x12(x+1)=2⋅5⋅x2⋅2⋅3⋅(x+1)

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of 2's.

2⋅5⋅x2⋅2⋅3⋅(x+1)=2⋅5⋅x2⋅2⋅3⋅(x+1)=5⋅x2⋅3⋅(x+1)=5x6(x+1)

Thus, the expression simplifies to 5x6(x+1).

q-100066.name: Question 6
q-100066.problem: What is $\frac{yz}{3xz}$ reduced to lowest terms?
q-100066.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{yz}{3xz}=\frac{y\cdot z}{3\cdot x\cdot z}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $z$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y\cdot z}{3\cdot x\cdot z} & = \\ \frac{y\cdot \cancel{z}}{3\cdot x\cdot \cancel{z}} & = \\ \frac{y}{3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{y}{3x}.$

q-67242.name: Question 7
q-67242.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{z(5+2z)}{3z}?$
q-67242.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z(5+2z)}{3z}=\frac{z\cdot (5+2z)}{3\cdot z}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $z$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z\cdot (5+2z)}{3\cdot z} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{z}\cdot (5+2z)}{3\cdot \cancel{z}} & = \\ \frac{5+2z}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{5+2z}{3}.$

Which of the following is equivalent to z(5+2z)3z?

a
5+2zz
b
2+2z3
c
5+5z3
d
2+5z3
e
5+2z3

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors.

z(5+2z)3z=z⋅(5+2z)3⋅z

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of z's.

z⋅(5+2z)3⋅z=z⋅(5+2z)3⋅z=5+2z3

Thus, the expression simplifies to 5+2z3.

q-41552.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $(3x)(7y)$ in the numerator becomes $3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y,$ and the $28y$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{(3x)(7y)}{28y}=\frac{3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y}{2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $7\text{'s}$ and one pair of $y$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3\cdot 7\cdot x\cdot y}{2\cdot 2\cdot 7\cdot y} & = \\ \frac{3\cdot \cancel{7}\cdot x\cdot \cancel{y}}{2\cdot 2\cdot \cancel{7}\cdot \cancel{y}} & = \\ \frac{3\cdot x}{2\cdot 2} & = \\ \frac{3}{4}x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{3}{4}x.$

q-14373.worked_solution:
First, we notice that $2x+3=3+2x.$ So we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3+2x}{2x+3}=\frac{3+2x}{3+2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $3+2x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3+2x}{3+2x} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{(3+2x)}}{\cancel{(3+2x)}} & = \\ 1\end{aligned}
$$

First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $3a(a-b)$ in the numerator becomes $3\cdot a\cdot (a-b),$ and the $9(a-b)$ in the denominator becomes $3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a(a-b)}{9(a-b)}=\frac{3\cdot a\cdot (a-b)}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $3$'s and one pair of $(a-b)$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3a(a-b)}{9(a-b)} & =\frac{3\cdot a\cdot (a-b)}{3\cdot 3\cdot (a-b)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{3}\cdot a\cdot \cancel{(a-b)}}{\cancel{3}\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{(a-b)}} \\  & =\frac{a}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{a}{3}.$
